section_title: Why does Nehemiah close the gates before the Sabbath?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 15 In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, and figs. All kinds of goods were being brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I warned them against selling food on that day. 16 Additionally, men of Tyre who lived there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem. 17 Then I rebuked the nobles of Judah and asked, “What is this evil you are doing—profaning the Sabbath day? 18 Did not your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? And now you are rekindling His wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath!”

19 When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates so that no load could enter on the Sabbath day. 20 Once or twice, the merchants and those who sell all kinds of goods camped outside Jerusalem, 21 but I warned them, “Why are you camping in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.” From that time on, they did not return on the Sabbath. 22 Then I instructed the Levites to purify themselves and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this as well, O my God, and show me mercy according to Your abundant loving devotion.

context_lines: Nehemiah sees winepresses being worked and loads of produce brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Traders from Tyre also sell fish and other goods to the people of Judah. These practices violate the commitment the people made in [Nehemiah 10:31](https://biblehub.com/bsb/nehemiah/10.htm).

He rebukes the nobles and reminds them that their ancestors’ disregard for the Sabbath contributed to the disaster that fell on the city. As evening shadows approach before the Sabbath, he orders the gates closed until it is over and stations his servants to stop loads entering.

When traders camp outside the wall, he warns them against returning. He also instructs the Levites to purify themselves and keep guard for the holiness of the Sabbath. His closing prayer asks God for remembrance and mercy according to His great loving devotion.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/nehemiah/13.htm) emphasizes the seriousness of disregarding the Sabbath after earlier judgment. [Gill](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/nehemiah/13.htm) also stresses the corrective action and understands the request for mercy as recognition that Nehemiah depends on God’s grace. Gill distinguishes the servants guarding the city gates from what he reads as the Levites’ responsibility at the temple gates. The account’s main concern is restoring observance of the time the community has promised to keep holy.
